validation-items._note: Documented follow-ups, NOT blockers. Phase 2A is approved with these open; each is resolved by evidence from the real world, not by a design decision.
validation-items.ko-ghorab-licence: Readex Pro stays the labelled Figma placeholder until the original licence terms or written vendor permission confirm that team/cloud font upload is allowed. KO Ghorab remains the approved PRODUCTION Arabic display typeface throughout.
validation-items.fold-safe-zones: DEVICE VALIDATION REQUIRED. The fold-landscape and youtube-landscape control bands and the fold-portrait reserves keep their derived values and are validated on real devices during production testing. They are not final measurements and were not invented as such.
validation-items.body-word-ceiling: The enforced slot rule is UNCHANGED at 18 Arabic words on every profile. Raising it for wide canvases is deferred and revisited during Static Ultra Carousel and Motion Carousel production testing.

$meta.authority: Figma file OD9bQi6eWexQi53tLKoctW defines the approved visual system. This file is the one machine-readable export automation consumes. It is GENERATED from site/src/styles/tokens by brand/scripts/build-tokens.mjs — never hand-edited.

signature-blue.role: primary brand colour, primary action, heart, links

deep-blue.role: pressed states, depth, text on Ice tint

fresh-mint.role: ACCENT ONLY — ≤ ~3% of any surface, never a background, never the logo

graphite.role: primary neutral, primary text, the everyday mark, dark-mode canvas

warm-white.role: primary light surface (page canvas), not pure white

neutral._note: Derived neutrals, NOT brand colours: interpolations on the Warm White → Graphite ramp that the UI needs.

muted.warning: NOT a text colour (2.46:1 on Warm White). Disabled controls, icon strokes, decorative rules only.

graphite-raised.source: documented composite of --adel-glass-fill (Graphite 0.94) over Warm White; the only dark raised surface with a written precedent

graphite-sunken.source: DERIVED, not invented: Graphite minus the measured canvas→raised step (+14/+13/+13), so the dark ladder sunken → canvas → raised is one even step in each direction. White text measures 19.48:1 on it.

status._note: Functional, not brand. Kept distinct from the blue family so correct/error/brand never read alike.

graphite-94.use: glass fill (the site header — the only glass surface)

dark._status: RESOLVED — Graphite-based dark surfaces. Values are either a documented precedent or a v2.1 semantic value newly introduced in the Phase 2A refinement, derived from the approved Graphite / Blue system and contrast-checked. Nothing is inherited from Dark Impact or Edition 1, and no arbitrary colour was added: exactly one new primitive (neutral/graphite-sunken) exists, everything else is an existing ramp step.
dark._contrast: Measured with the WCAG relative-luminance formula. Text pairs clear 4.5:1; UI fills clear 3:1 against the surface they sit on.

sunken.derivation: Graphite − the canvas→raised step, mirroring the light ladder downward

tint.derivation: the published blue ramp's darkest step — the dark counterpart of Ice Blue, from the approved ramp rather than a new mix

link.precedent: LoveTech .lovetech--onDark; Signature Blue is 3.37:1 on Graphite and fails 4.5:1 for text

action._rule: The light ladder's rule is "each state moves one step further from the surface". On a Graphite surface that direction is LIGHTER, so the dark ladder is the same rule mirrored — and the foreground flips to Graphite because the fill is now the light element. This is not a preference: keeping the light ladder on dark fails the 3:1 UI floor against the canvas (blue/600 = 2.63:1, deep-blue = 2.02:1), so the mirrored ladder is the accessible option.

primary-fg.note: Graphite, not White: on dark the primary fill is a light blue, so the label inverts with it. White on blue/400 measures 3.17:1 and fails.

expressive._status: APPROVED SECONDARY — expressive / creator palette. Never replaces Signature Blue as the primary brand colour, never used on the logo, the website UI, navigation, core layouts or official brand surfaces.
_rules: Controlled accents and expressive content colour — never a random or decorative choice.
One expressive hue leads a given piece; a second appears only when the content genuinely has two sides (A/B, before/after, correct/wrong).
Never on the mark, the lockups, the I ❤ Tech heart, the signature, or any website/app UI surface.
Never a substitute for a status colour: correct and error stay functional green/red.
The -700 steps are the text-safe members; the -500 steps are graphic.
Same values in Figma, Canva and video — the expressive palette is one system, not a per-tool improvisation.
Gradients stay retired: the expressive palette is flat colour.

signal-blue._note: Electric / Signal Blue. Distinct from Signature Blue #2563EB and never used where the brand blue belongs — pair them only with a clear reason.

lavender._note: Atmosphere tints for expressive grounds only.

archived._note: Edition 1 / ATT Content System — what stays archived after the expressive reclassification. Not deleted. Scoped to .att-legacy in the site; Figma page 99. Never used in active work.

dark-impact._note: Dark Impact mode and its 45° three-stop gradient. Retired: the active system approves no gradient and dark surfaces are Graphite-based.

violet-neutrals._note: Violet-tinted neutral ramp. Replaced by the hueless Graphite → Warm White ramp.

violet-elevation._note: Violet shadow ladder. Replaced by the neutral-cool Graphite ladder.

archived.display-face: Cairo — Edition 1 Arabic display; KO Ghorab replaces it on every social and video surface.

pillar-hues._note: The five-colour content-pillar system (teal / pink / gold) is not revived: topics are differentiated by their label, not by hue. Magenta returns only through the expressive palette above, and never as a pillar.

display.job: Latin display — standalone headings, wordmarks, nav, CTA, index figures. Never inside an Arabic run.

text.stack: 'Readex Pro', 'Segoe UI', Tahoma, 'Noto Sans Arabic', sans-serif
text.job: Arabic body/UI, any Latin inside an Arabic sentence, EN long-form.

arabic-display.job: Arabic display only — hero, headings, pull quotes. ≥ 24 px. Never letter-spaced. Single weight: hierarchy by size.
arabic-display.licence: licensed to Adel; self-hosted; NOT redistributable
arabic-display.licence-terms: NOT STORED WITH THE PROJECT — no EULA, licence file or written grant exists anywhere in the repository; site/src/assets/fonts/README.md asserts the licence but does not reproduce its terms.
arabic-display.figma: NOT UPLOADED. A Figma team-font upload puts the file on the Figma servers and shares it with every team member, which is a redistribution-shaped use. The stored licence does not clearly permit it, so it is not done. KO Ghorab remains the approved Arabic display face and stays in production and export use where the licence does permit it (self-hosted on the site, and in local rendering). The Figma [Ghorab] styles keep their labelled Readex Pro placeholder family. No other typeface substitutes for Ghorab.

hand.job: About-page sketch layer ONLY, EN only. Placeholder until real handwriting exists. NEVER a signature stand-in.

removed-from-core.AR/UI: Readex Pro Medium 14/24. Removed from the canonical core typography system in the Phase 2A refinement: no site token backs it and nothing in production uses it. Preserved in Figma only as "Legacy / AR-UI (reference only)", not a brand standard. Arabic compact UI takes the EN/Label size with the Arabic body face.

not-approved.Tajawal: generic skill example — not brand data
not-approved.Amiri: not core; documented exception only for the scripture line on the holding page (coming-soon.astro)

rules: RTL-first layouts; Latin terms are isolated LTR islands (.term)
no uppercase concept — overlines are sentence case
Ghorab has no Latin glyphs: an English term inside a Ghorab headline falls to Montserrat 700 at ×0.925

social._note: Authored in Arabic. Latin steps DOWN: size ÷ 1.08, line-height − 0.15. cover = KO Ghorab (was Cairo) · title/sub/body/support/label = Readex Pro · spec = JetBrains Mono tabular · index = Montserrat

elevation._note: neutral-cool Graphite shadows; the violet ladder is archived

canvases._note: reserve-top / reserve-bottom are layout reserves: no headline, body or signature inside them. They are larger than, and contain, the platform UI-overlay areas the video skill's safe-check detects.

reel-9x16.label: Reel / Story 9:16
reel-9x16.use: Motion Carousel slides, Reels, ASMR, Talking Head, all vertical video

slots._note: ENFORCED, counted in Arabic words. On breach the remedy is fewer words, never smaller type.

canvasProfiles._note: Canonical VIDEO device profiles for the Adaptive / Fold-First Content System. APPROVED ARCHITECTURE (Phase 2A final). All four are AdelTechTalks — one identity, four compositions. Dimensions are configuration, never assumptions baked into an editor.
canvasProfiles._validation: DEVICE VALIDATION REQUIRED on the fold and landscape safe zones: the derived values below stand as working values and are confirmed on real devices during production testing. The architecture is approved; those measurements are not yet final.
_contract: RECOMPOSITION, not resize or crop. A profile re-lays-out the same source edit: subject framing, product placement, text position and line length, captions, brand position, safe zones and motion are all profile-aware.
Never produce a fold profile by centre-cropping or letterboxing the 9:16 master.
Graphics EXPAND into the extra canvas; they are not scaled up to fill it.
Extra canvas is a reason to give content room, not a reason to add content. Empty space is a legitimate use of it.
No profile gets its own visual identity: same palette, same faces, same mark roles, same motion charter.
A profile is requested, never forced: one, several, or the full Adaptive Device Pack.

captionRegion._note: Between the focal column and the bottom reserve; the reference composition ends the caption card at y 1460.

focal.rule: Face, hands, product or action stay inside the content area between the reserves; never let the focal subject enter a reserve.

foldPortrait.label: Fold Portrait
foldPortrait.provenance: DEVICE VALIDATION REQUIRED — margin derived from the audited reel ratio; reserves derived from the audited Feed 4:5 reserves × 1.4222

grid._note: Two more columns than the 9:16 reel: the extra width is for a second content column, not a wider single column.

captionRegion._note: Captions keep the reel line length rather than stretching to the full fold width — a longer caption line is harder to read, not better.

textLimits.revisit: The enforced ceiling stays 18 Arabic words on every profile. Raising it to 24 for the wider measure was proposed and is DEFERRED — revisited during Static Ultra Carousel and Motion Carousel production testing. Headline and title ceilings do not rise at all: a bigger canvas is not a licence for a longer headline, and "fewer words, never smaller type" still governs a breach.

focal.rule: The focal subject keeps the dominant column at its 9:16 scale; the freed width becomes a real second zone (graphic, product, spec, B-roll) or deliberate breathing room.

foldLandscape.label: Fold Landscape
foldLandscape.provenance: DEVICE VALIDATION REQUIRED — margin derived from the audited reel ratio; no audited landscape VIDEO reserve exists, so the bottom band is a working value to confirm on device

captionRegion._note: Landscape captions sit as a lower-third band, not a full-width strip.

textLimits.revisit: Enforced ceiling unchanged at 18 Arabic words; the rise to 24 for the wider measure is DEFERRED and revisited during Static Ultra Carousel and Motion Carousel production testing.

youtubeLandscape._note: Fold-first does not replace standard YouTube. This profile stays first-class.

focal.layout: focal subject + supporting zone, or full-frame for demo footage
focal.rule: Long-form framing: the focal subject may sit off-centre with the supporting zone carrying the explainer graphic.

adaptiveLayouts._note: Recomposition rules per production format. PRIMARY never crops; SECONDARY moves, resizes or reflows; TEXT ZONE and BRAND ZONE are profile-dependent; FOCAL ZONE is what a naive crop would destroy.

talking-head.primary: the speaker — face and gesture space, uncropped
talking-head.secondary: B-roll insert, contextual graphic, semantic scene cards, progress bar
talking-head.textZone: caption card in the caption region; semantic scene text in the supporting zone on fold profiles
talking-head.brandZone: handle badge below the top reserve; signature micro, bottom
talking-head.focalZone: face and upper body, plus the hand area when the speaker gestures — never blind-crop either

profiles.verticalStandard: speaker in the single focal column; scene graphics overlay or tuck under the caption card.
profiles.foldPortrait: speaker keeps the dominant column at 9:16 scale; the second column takes the contextual graphic, product still or transcript panel. Do NOT enlarge the speaker to fill 3:4.
profiles.foldLandscape: speaker + supporting visual side by side, or speaker with intentional breathing room. The graphic becomes a real panel, not an overlay.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: speaker off-centre with the explainer graphic in the supporting zone; captions as a lower third.

product-hero.primary: the product — silhouette and finish, uncropped, visually dominant
product-hero.textZone: opposite the product mass; never across the product
product-hero.brandZone: corner furthest from the product, micro scale
product-hero.focalZone: the product outline plus its highlight and shadow contact — a crop that clips either reads as damage

profiles.verticalStandard: product centred, text above or below it.
profiles.foldPortrait: product holds one column, headline and spec stack in the other.
profiles.foldLandscape: product leading, text trailing (mirrored for RTL); the extra width is space around the product, not a bigger product.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: product with room for an on-screen spec or callout.

talking-head-plus-broll.primary: speech is the spine — the speaker and the synchronised B-roll moment
talking-head-plus-broll.secondary: which of the two is foregrounded at a given beat
talking-head-plus-broll.textZone: caption card, tied to word timing
talking-head-plus-broll.focalZone: the speaker face and the B-roll subject; one of the two is always fully visible

profiles.verticalStandard: cut between speaker and B-roll, or B-roll inside a card over the speaker.
profiles.foldPortrait: both can coexist — speaker column + B-roll column — so the cut becomes a choice, not a necessity.
profiles.foldLandscape: speaker and B-roll genuinely side by side; the caption spans under both.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: picture-in-picture or split, speaker smaller when the B-roll carries the point.

comparison-ab.primary: both products, at matched scale and matched framing
comparison-ab.secondary: labels, spec rows, verdict card, scorecard
comparison-ab.textZone: product labels stay pinned to their side; verdict text in the shared zone
comparison-ab.brandZone: neutral corner, never inside either product half
comparison-ab.focalZone: the compared feature area on each product — the thing the comparison is about

profiles.verticalStandard: stacked A over B, or A → B in sequence; split-screen only when simultaneity matters.
profiles.foldPortrait: true side-by-side becomes comfortable; labels sit above each column.
profiles.foldLandscape: the best canvas for this format — large side-by-side A/B at equal scale, spec row beneath, verdict card in the shared band.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: side-by-side with a persistent spec strip.

asmr-unboxing.primary: the tactile action — hands, packaging, the product surface
asmr-unboxing.textZone: minimal or none; brand text only
asmr-unboxing.brandZone: micro signature, corner, late in the edit
asmr-unboxing.focalZone: the hands and the contact point where the sound is made

profiles.verticalStandard: action fills the focal column, clean.
profiles.foldPortrait: keep the action LARGE and the frame clean. Extra canvas is breathing room around the action — do not add graphics because space exists.
profiles.foldLandscape: wider view of the surface and the hands; still no added graphics, no music, no captions by default.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: longer-form unboxing framing; the recorded tactile audio remains the point.

asmr-unboxing.rule: The ASMR audio policy is profile-independent: recorded tactile audio stays ON, no music, captions, denoise, gating or compression by default.

product-demo.primary: the feature in real use — the proof shot
product-demo.textZone: callout beside the action on wide profiles; overlaid only when there is no room
product-demo.focalZone: the interaction point — the control being pressed, the screen being shown, the result appearing

profiles.verticalStandard: callout overlays or follows the action.
profiles.foldPortrait: product and feature callout COEXIST — the callout stops being an overlay and becomes its own zone.
profiles.foldLandscape: demo footage leading, callout stack trailing; steps can persist instead of flashing.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: screen recording or proof shot with a persistent callout column.

motion-carousel.primary: the slide media — one idea per slide, product/video first
motion-carousel.brandZone: micro signature, consistent corner across all slides
motion-carousel.focalZone: the slide subject; each slide must read alone

profiles.verticalStandard: the canonical slide: 1080×1920, ~5 s, own MP4.
profiles.foldPortrait: FOLD EDITION — each slide is RECOMPOSED for the wider canvas: media and text become two zones rather than a stack. Never a crop of the 9:16 slide.
profiles.foldLandscape: fold edition in landscape; slide motion may use the horizontal axis (parallax, reveal) that 9:16 cannot afford.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: the stitched preview is the natural 16:9 artefact; individual slides stay social.

motion-carousel.rule: Every profile still exports each slide as its own MP4; the stitched preview stays optional.

long-form-explainer.primary: the explanation — speaker, screen recording or diagram, whichever carries the point
long-form-explainer.secondary: chapter cards, lower thirds, recurring diagram
long-form-explainer.focalZone: the diagram or screen region being discussed

profiles.foldPortrait: speaker + diagram stack, comfortable for a handheld unfolded read.
profiles.foldLandscape: large diagram with the speaker inset.
profiles.youtubeLandscape: the home profile for this format.

adaptiveMigration.principle: The editor must not hold a canvas assumption anywhere. A dimension is configuration, read from a profile, at every stage: analysis, cut, zoom, compose, caption, safe-check, encode.

foldFirstNaming.status: RESERVED CONCEPT ONLY — not an official badge, not a permanent brand element.
foldFirstNaming.rule: Consumer-facing language is reserved, not adopted. Nothing ships with these words until a separate decision approves one.

reversed.name: White
reversed.use: dark or photographic grounds; never tinted grey

adeltechtalks.direction: ltr, never mirrored, Latin on the Arabic site too

signature.rule: No handwritten signature is created, simulated, traced or set in a handwriting font. The slot stays empty until Adel supplies a real scanned signature (SVG or transparent PNG).

video-end-card.rule: When the real scan exists, the video end card gains a signature variant that a job may choose. It is never applied automatically and never becomes a required element on every video. The default end card carries the mark or lockup, not the signature.
video-end-card.applies-to: every canvas profile; the signature follows the profile brand zone and stays micro scale

colour: Never invent a brand colour when an approved token exists.
Signature Blue is the primary brand colour everywhere; the expressive palette never replaces it.

Core palette on the logo, website/UI, navigation, core layouts and official brand surfaces. Expressive palette only on creator content: motion carousels, playground/gamification, badges, AI/tech explainers, thumbnails, campaign moments, accents.
Fresh Mint ≤ ~3% of any surface; never a background, never the logo.
No gradients anywhere in the active system, expressive palette included.
Status colours are functional, never brand and never replaced by an expressive hue.
logo: One geometry, three colour roles (Graphite / Signature Blue / White). Never stretch, redraw, recolour or add a gradient tile.
AdelTechTalks lockup is primary; Adel lockup is secondary.
Bare mark never below 24 px; below that use an app-icon tile.
typography: Montserrat when Latin stands alone; Readex Pro the moment Latin sits inside an Arabic sentence.
KO Ghorab: Arabic display only, ≥ 24 px, never letter-spaced, hierarchy by size.
Arabic layouts RTL-first with isolated LTR islands for Latin terms.
video: Product footage occupies the dominant area; text second; signature micro.
ASMR: recorded tactile audio (box opening, peeling, clicks, scratches, packaging, handling) stays ON — no music, captions, denoise, gating or compression by default, in every canvas profile.
Motion Carousel: 5–6 independent ~5 s slides at 1080×1920, each exportable as its own MP4; a stitched preview is optional; never a static carousel with generic zoom.
Brand opener / end card are micro moments, not intros.
Motion is precise and premium, not template-heavy: cut / match-cut by default for ASMR.
Adaptive profiles RECOMPOSE; they never centre-crop or letterbox the 9:16 master. Graphics expand into the canvas rather than scaling up to fill it.
Extra canvas is room for the same content, not a reason to add content — ASMR in particular stays clean.
Canvas dimensions are configuration read from canvasProfiles, never assumptions held inside the editor.
